record: adversarial review of the prepared static-only nested refinement study, revision 1
method: five independent read-only reviewers (certificate mathematics, classification theory, driver and evidence, solver numerics, claims and consistency), then one independent verifier per lens for every blocking or major finding; CLAUDE.md 7.1 applied: a finding is refuted only by demonstrating on the snapshot that the defect does not exist
note: Reviewer agreement is not evidence by itself. Two reviewers read the QMHP level-0 mesh geometry, and one computed an assembly-only statistic (1^T|K|1) from it; no reviewer ran a solve, capacitance or energy computation on the QMHP mesh.

findings.title: The preconditions do not require a non-overlapping mesh: a folded mesh passes every check and the bound understates its error 1.8-5x
findings.claim: The proof needs the tetrahedra to tile a region inside B without overlap. Volumes are |det| (anchor_fem._tet_geometry), so overlapping or inverted tetrahedra cannot be seen. The docstring's promise, 'Empty means it is [rigorous]', is therefore false in general.

findings.title: The assembled K is not symmetric, but the energy identity and the residual bound assume it is
findings.claim: E(phi~) - E_h = r^T A^-1 r needs A = A^T and K_fD = K_Df^T. p1_stiffness assembles through COO to CSR, which sums duplicate entries in different orders for (i,j) and (j,i), so K is not symmetric at the ulp level. The energy phi^T K phi sees only sym(K). The residual of the problem the energy actually minimises is therefore r_s = r - 1/2 (A - A^T) x - 1/2 (K_fD - K_Df^T) phi_D, and g does not include that term. So 'relative to the assembled matrix' does not describe the problem that was proved.

checked_and_found_sound: Energy identity: with the Dirichlet values imposed exactly, E(x) - E(x*) = (x - x*)^T A (x - x*) = r^T A^-1 r >= 0 for any x (given A symmetric; see CM-3). So an inexact solve can only raise the energy, for C and for C'. The feasible set of C' is inside that of C, so E'_h >= E_h. The float Dirichlet values of C' define that problem.
The Loewner step A >= c D_m implies A^-1 <= (c D_m)^-1, which gives the bound sum r_i^2/m_i/c.

The element mass vol/20 (I + 11^T) is >= vol/20 I, and this holds on the free-node restriction because fixed entries are zero. nodal_mass_lower's np.repeat(vol/20, 4) lines up with tets.ravel(). Committed V5b shows min eig(M - D_m) = 5.2e-8 >= 0.
eps_min is taken over np.unique(tet_attr), the attributes that actually occur, using the same eps_r dict as p1_stiffness.
Scaling is consistent: K (length^1), m (length^3) and lambda_1 (length^-2) are all computed on xyz_nd. The QMHP box extents [1, 1, 0.4825] give lambda_1 = 62.133, matching preflight.json.
The bounding box is taken over all nodes. Unused nodes can only enlarge B and lower c, which is conservative. Unused nodes are excluded from the free set, and QMHP level 0 has none.

Boundary nodes are derived from single-use tetrahedron faces, not from the tags, so any untagged, hanging-node or crack face shows up and its nodes must be fixed. A boundary node on the island (fixed at 1) is still zero in the homogeneous error. For C, a port-tagged face on the outer boundary would be flagged. The face-key overflow guard holds at level 2 (n^3 = 3.6e17 < 2^63).

Residual rounding: gamma(kA+1)(|b| + |A||x|) + gamma(kD)|K_fD||phi_D| is the standard componentwise bound for any summation order, including FMA. kA and kD come from stored row lengths, which is conservative.
BOUND_SAFETY = 1.001 covers the float evaluation of sum rb^2/m (gamma_n about 6.5e-11 at 5.8e5 unknowns) and of c and m for any non-pathological element.

The evaluation-error bound |e64 - eld64| + u64|eld64| + gamma_{n+k}(u_ld)|phi|^T|K||phi| is an upper bound. The nested-dot bound is standard. The Sterbenz subtraction is exact. I confirmed that scipy 1.17.1's longdouble sparse matvec and numpy's longdouble dot accumulate in 80-bit (1 + 1e-17 - 1 = 9.97e-18). An exact rational evaluation on chip-cell levels 0-1 puts the actual error at 0.9-7.5% of the bound.
require_extended_precision is called before preflight and execute. ULD is read from finfo, so the bound stays valid even without extended precision.

The relative bound total/(E - total) and the interval [E - total, E + total] point the right way. S_2/(1 + rel) <= k/(E + total) <= S_h, and C_2(1 + rel) >= eps0 Lc (E + evalerr), both valid up to the assembly round-off in CM-2.

PCG's stopping test uses only the residual term (target 1e-12). The final integrity check adds the evaluation term. The level-2 residual floor (1.1e-15 nd, about 5e-16 relative) is far below 1e-12, so CERTIFIED is reachable.

The QMHP level-0 mesh (geometry only) has all 64,434 tets positively oriented, with sum|vol| equal to the bounding-box volume, so the folding gap in CM-1 does not apply to the ladder. Red refinement partitions each parent.

review.summary:
I reviewed frozen snapshot 864c0baef389bbe0a45345b7b27cf74f8afd17c4, read-only. I ran no solve, assembly, capacitance or energy computation on the QMHP mesh. The only QMHP access was reading the level-0 mesh geometry and reading the pinned Palace CSVs and config. All experiments were synthetic calls to classify(), analyse() and consistency() using fabricated level records. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-QMHP-CEM/7e301b81-9cc3-5878-8c8a-f1390dcdb988/scratchpad/review/classification-theory/ (t1.py to t6.py, geo.py).

The core mathematics holds:
- I re-derived the two-term model bracket and it is correct. It also holds for any positive combination of orders >= 1.
- The r^(1/2) exponent survives for a sheet lying in the dielectric interface plane, and all sheets and the port are at z=0, on that interface.
- The C_2 intervals and the 0.1215 floor are right.
- Recomputing the consistency window from the pinned CSVs reproduces the frozen window exactly.
- |p| is the correct participation: it equals E_ind/E_elec from domain-E.csv to <= 4.3e-10, and the sign follows Im V.
- The outcome is not predetermined: C's class depends on the unknown C_2.

Defects found:
- (1) Code and pre-declaration disagree. The pre-declaration says that on an INCONSISTENT or UNRESOLVED consistency verdict H_h is reported only as S'_h and labelled 'identity not confirmed'. analyse() never does this: the relabelling was shown to be missing.
- (2) The level-0 consistency check needs only level-0 data, yet any integrity failure or exception at any level suppresses it, and the pre-declaration forbids recovering it afterwards. A failure confined to level 2 (the untried PCG solve) would therefore forfeit the study's one sharp cross-code test. Demonstrated.
- (3) The documents call the identity 'verified' and H_h 'Palace's complete harmonic moment', and list delta_0 >= 6.585e-4 as already known. The identity has only been checked against the project's own reimplementation of Palace's port; the level-0 check is its first test against Palace.
- (4) The theory text and the reason strings mislabel the window edges. R slightly below 2 is exactly what theory predicts when the higher-order coefficient is negative, but it is labelled 'slower than the theoretical leading order'. R > 4 is labelled 'faster than any P1 order', which is false.
- (5) The delta class reuses energy-theory reason strings and model brackets, and can print CONVERGED 'rate consistent with theory' for delta, although no rate theory exists for it.
- (6) The C' and H classes carry almost no information beyond C's class.
- (7) The pre-declaration says tau 'constrains C''. In practice CONVERGED is unreachable for C' as well.
- (8) The eta derivation treats a backward error as if it were a forward error. The eta budget itself is adequate.

None of these is blocking in the sense of making a successful run useless. Findings 1 to 3 are major because a stated guarantee or claim is false.

findings.title: The level-0 consistency check is forfeited by any failure at levels 1-2, and may not be recovered afterwards
findings.claim: The consistency verdict depends only on the level-0 energies and the pinned band. analyse() computes it only after integrity() passes for all three levels. On any exception after the record exists, execute() writes failure.json and runs no analysis at all. The pre-declaration then forbids reading a verdict from the preserved raw data ('no class and no consistency verdict is read from it'). A failure confined to level 2 therefore spends the single attempt and loses the study's one sharp two-code test, even when level 0 completed and passed every level-0 check. Level 2 is the only solver path never run on the QMHP operator: PCG STAGNATED or MAXITER, an RLIMIT_AS MemoryError, or a SIGALRM wall-clock stop.

findings.title: The window and its labels overstate what the theory fixes: the sign assumption is unsupported and the R>4 and R<2 labels are wrong
findings.claim:
The theory forces the leading coefficient a > 0, but it does not fix the sign of the higher-order terms. For a > 0 and b < 0 the two-term model always gives R < 2, in the genuine order-1 regime. That case is classified UNRESOLVED with the reason 'slower than the theoretical leading order 1', and the documents label 50.07-66.13 fF 'UNRESOLVED (slower than order 1)'. Two plausible mechanisms give b < 0:
(i) the edge-vertex cutoff. The edge intensity ~ rho^(lambda-1/2) near a plate corner gives a h - (kappa_e c0^2/(2 lambda)) h^(2 lambda+1) + kappa_v h^(2 lambda+1).
(ii) the element-shape population change under red refinement of a Gmsh mesh. Level 0 is all Gmsh shapes; half of level 1 is octahedron children. With a_0 = a(1+eps) this acts as an h^2 term of either sign and shifts R by 4 eps.
Conversely, R > 4 is labelled 'faster than any order a P1 energy error can have', and 'No P1 energy term is faster than h^2' is false: higher-order terms exist, and a h + c h^3 gives R = 7.7. Finally, with the theory's own list of orders (1, 1.5, 2) and mixed signs, R in [2,4] does not imply the bracket. The pre-declaration does say that the bracket assumes the two-term model.

checked_and_found_sound:
The two-term bracket, re-derived. For X_h = X + a h + b h^q (h = 1, 1/2, 1/4, u = 2^-q):
- d1 = a/2 + b(1-u) and d2 = a/4 + b u(1-u). R is the mediant of 2 and 2^q with weights a/4 and b u(1-u), so a, b >= 0 gives R in [2, 2^q], a subset of [2, 4].
- The level-2 error e2 = a/4 + b u^2 satisfies d2 - e2 = b 4^-q (2^q - 2) >= 0 for q >= 1, and e2(d1-d2) - d2^2 = (a/4) b (1-2u)^2 >= 0.
- So the true limit lies in [X2 - d2, X2 - d2/(R-1)] as claimed. This extends, via Cauchy-Schwarz, to any positive combination of orders >= 1: 20,000 random trials, 0 violations (t2.py (d)). The [2,4] window is not needed for the bracket itself.

The sheet-edge exponent. For a sheet lying in the eps interface plane, continuity of u and of eps du/dtheta gives cos(lambda pi)(eps1+eps2) = 0, so lambda = 1/2 and the energy error is O(h). Geometry read from the level-0 mesh (no assembly): every conductor-sheet triangle (attr 4), the port (10) and attrs 11-12 lie at z=0. That is the eps interface (20,944 attr-1/attr-3 faces, all at z=0; substrate z in [-0.43, 0]). The outer walls (attr 2) meet the interface at right angles with Dirichlet data, which is regular.
The vertex order 2 lambda + 1 lies in (1, 2) for any lambda in (0, 1/2), so the window does not depend on the uncertain corner exponent, including its shift from the eps contrast.

The C_2 intervals: C1 - d1 = 50.0656, C1 - d1/2 = 66.1339, C1 - d1/4 = 74.1680. The CONVERGED floor d1/(4 C1 - 2 d1) = 0.1215 is correct. The 34 selected rule and consistency tests pass on the snapshot.

The consistency window, recomputed from the pinned CSVs (digests 11c19784... and ed5dbf60... match): sum|p|/f^2 = 0.46730189366826225, N_B = 0.999373878899728, f_max = 8.706861807, delta_band = 6.58526684468308e-4, tail = 1.768574651809676e-5, window [6.585166844683079e-4, 6.762224309864047e-4]. |p| is the correct participation. |p_j| equals E_ind/E_elec from domain-E.csv to <= 4.3e-10 for all six modes, and sign(p_j) = sign(Im V_j), which is the phase convention (matching the repo's GetInductorParticipation model in tests/test_first_moment_diagnostic.py:898). review.summary:
I reviewed snapshot 864c0baef389bbe0a45345b7b27cf74f8afd17c4 read-only. I ran nothing on the QMHP mesh, created no approval, wrote nothing under results/, and ran study_driver.py only through synthetic harnesses in which every QMHP input was stubbed. The harnesses are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-QMHP-CEM/7e301b81-9cc3-5878-8c8a-f1390dcdb988/scratchpad/review/driver-evidence/ (gate.py, h1*, h2, h3, h4*, h5, h6).

The main path is sound. Every refusal I could construct runs before the record directory exists. Raw level files are written before analysis. On the real pinned inputs, band_baseline and anchor_values reproduce the frozen values exactly. The S = k/E unit derivation is valid to 1.6e-16. In 20 of 20 trials, a real SIGXCPU budget stop left failure.json and a verified manifest.

I found no defect that would certainly waste the attempt.

I found four major problems:
1. **A completed, certified C_2 solve is thrown away if the C'_2 solve raises.** The level record is written only after every solve on that level. Demonstrated.
2. **"failure.json and a verified manifest on every path" is false.** It fails when memory runs out in small allocations under RLIMIT_AS (demonstrated), when write_verified raises on the success path, and on the kernel and outer-timeout SIGKILL paths. The consequences of those kill paths are not disclosed. Each path is low-probability.
3. **The one-attempt rule only looks at the results/ folder of the checkout that runs it.** The approval carries no attempt number, validity window or consumption marker, so a second checkout at the approving commit gets a second attempt. Demonstrated.
4. **The approval binds only 4 files, although it claims to bind every code file.** 30 other repository modules run in the same process through orchestrator/__init__.py and are not bound. None has an import-time side effect today.

I also found five minor issues:
- failure.json records no provenance.
- level1.json and level2.json always contain the non-standard JSON token Infinity.
- The port voltage of the level-1 cross-check is not checked, although the predeclaration says it is checked for every solve.
- The already-known C_0/C_1 reproduction and the deterministic two-grid refusals are checked only after the attempt is spent.
- The worst-case CPU estimate is understated. It is about 35 min rather than 26, still inside the 60-min cap, and it depends on the thread count.

review.summary:
I reviewed snapshot 864c0baef389bbe0a45345b7b27cf74f8afd17c4 (read-only worktree). Every experiment used synthetic chip_cell meshes. I read no QMHP data, ran no solve on the QMHP mesh, and did not run study_driver.py. The scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-QMHP-CEM/7e301b81-9cc3-5878-8c8a-f1390dcdb988/scratchpad/review/solver-numerics/ (e1-e9).

The level-2 solver is mathematically sound, and I found no blocking defect.
- trans='T' does perform the backward sweep with the upper triangle.
- The two-grid cycle is symmetric (asymmetry about 1e-16) and positive definite.
- The prolongation matches refine_red bit for bit.
- The target of 1e-12 can be reached. On synthetic cells the certificate levels off about 8 orders below it, and the QMHP proxy floor is about 3 orders below it.

Iteration counts rise with element anisotropy: 65-185 iterations up to aspect p99 75, and 415-540 at aspect p99 210-278. The QMHP mesh has aspect p99 17 and max 34 at level 2, so maxiter 1000 leaves a large margin. That iteration count on the real operator is still unmeasured.

The findings are minor but real, and each could turn a run that is still converging, or already acceptable, into a spent attempt, or weaken the evidence:
1. The stagnation rule counts infinite certificates as 'no improvement'. On synthetic cells the infinite phase used up to 15 of the 20 allowed checks on a solve that later reached CERTIFIED.
2. CERTIFIED at 1e-12 is required even though the declared tolerance is 1e-9.
3. If a later solve in the same level fails, results already completed in that level are thrown away (reproduced).
4. The Gauss-Seidel probe checks only the forward solve, is not run in preflight, and is declared as an integrity tolerance but raises a Refusal that spends the attempt.
5. The 'residual' column in the recorded history is the recursive residual, not the true residual.

findings.title: Stagnation rule counts infinite certificates as non-improvement, so a solve that is still converging can be declared STAGNATED
findings.claim: pcg() starts with best = inf and never seeds it. It tests `rel < 0.9 * best`, and inf < inf is False. So every check where the loose certificate still exceeds the energy (certify returns inf when e <= bnd) adds to `since`. With the frozen stagnation_checks=20 and check_every=5, a solve whose certificate stays above E for 100 iterations is declared STAGNATED, even while its A-norm error is falling. The certificate can also go back to inf after being finite, because PCG residuals are not monotone.
findings.evidence: nested_solver.py:350 (best = math.inf), :370-376 (improvement test and since counter), :455 (certify returns inf when e <= bnd), :388-389 (SOLVER settings). No test runs the STAGNATED branch: tests/test_static_refinement_study.py only fakes the status string at :311. At the prolonged initial guess the certificate is 3e4-1.1e5 times E, roughly doubling per level (e4_cert0.py: 46211 to 107083, 35755 to 68479, 30529 to 60532 for levels 1 to 2).
findings.reproduction:
Ran e3_hist.py under the frozen settings. Number of infinite checks out of the 20 allowed:
- dry-run cell {h0:.02,q:1.6,hmax:.5}, level 1: 2 (CERTIFIED at 85)
- {h0:.1,q:3,split}, level 2: 3 (120)
- {h0:.04,q:4,hmax:1.5}, level 2: 3 (90)
- {h0:.05,q:5,hmax:2,split}, level 2: 4 (150)
- {h0:.01,q:4}, level 1, aspect p99 75: 6 (185)
- {h0:.005,q:6}, level 1, aspect p99 210: 13 (415)
- {h0:.004,q:8,hmax:1.5}, level 1, aspect p99 278: 15 (k=0..70 all inf; CERTIFIED at 540)
In the last run the certificate also returned to inf after being finite: k=85 0.991, k=90 32.7, k=95 inf.
findings.consequence: STAGNATED is an integrity failure, so the record becomes UNQUALIFIED and the single attempt is spent even though the solve would have certified. At QMHP-like quality (p99 17) the synthetic margin is about 14-17 checks, so this is unlikely on the real mesh. However, the level-2 infinite phase on the QMHP operator has not been measured (preflight cannot compute it, and dry_run.json keeps no histories). The guarantee that STAGNATED means stagnation is not strictly true.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the stagnation count only after the first finite certificate, or seed best with it. Alternatively, base stagnation on a quantity that is monotone in exact PCG, such as the energy decrease. Add a test of the STAGNATED branch, including an infinite-then-finite certificate. Record the full level-2 history of the dry run.

findings.title: A solve that meets the declared 1e-9 tolerance is still an integrity failure unless it reaches 1e-12
findings.claim: _solver_problems requires status == CERTIFIED, which means the relative certificate reached target_rel = 1e-12. The declared integrity tolerance on every energy is certificate_rel_tol = 1e-9. A two-grid solve that is rigorously certified below 1e-9 but stops at MAXITER or STAGNATED before 1e-12 therefore makes the record UNQUALIFIED, even though its value meets every declared accuracy requirement.
findings.evidence: study_driver.py:225-226 (status must be CERTIFIED), :249 (certificate_rel_tol); predeclaration.json:106 (target_rel 1e-12), :109 ('Anything but CERTIFIED is an integrity failure'), :114 (certificate_rel_tol 1e-9).
findings.reproduction:
From the synthetic histories (e3_hist.py), the iteration where the certificate first reaches about 1e-9 versus the iteration where it reaches 1e-12:
- dry-run cell, level 1: k=65 (5.4e-10) vs k=85
- small cell, level 2: k=95 (5.8e-10) vs k=120
- aspect-330 cell: k=445 (9.5e-10) vs k=540
The extra 3 orders cost about 20-25% more iterations, and every one of those iterations sits inside the window where MAXITER or STAGNATED would void an already acceptable result.
findings.consequence: This is a failure mode the declared tolerance does not need, and it can spend the one attempt for no scientific reason. The rule was declared in advance, so it is not hidden, but it makes the attempt more fragile than the stated tolerances imply.
findings.suggested_fix: Judge integrity on the certificate (total_error_bound_rel <= certificate_rel_tol) and keep the PCG status as a recorded diagnostic. Otherwise, state in the pre-declaration why a solve certified at 1e-9 but not CERTIFIED must still be UNQUALIFIED.

findings.title: If a later solve in the same level fails, results already completed in that level are discarded
findings.claim: run_levels writes a level's record only after both problems (and, at level 1, both two-grid cross-checks) have finished. If a later solve in the same level raises, the completed results are lost. Examples: the level-1 cross-check raises (a TwoGrid Refusal, MemoryError under RLIMIT_AS, or BudgetExceeded), or the level-2 C' solve raises after level-2 C has finished.
